newsitem.title: USA: U.S. investors shun Australis junk deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investors shun Australis junk deal.

text.p: U.S. high-yield investors showed little interest in a $150 million 144a private placement offering of high-yield zero coupon bonds by Australis Media Ltd, which hit the market on Tuesday, market sources said.
Accordingly, underwriters Salomon Brothers Inc and Toronto Dominion (USA) Inc were forced to buy a significant portion of the deal themselves, the sources added.

"The company has had an unpleasant saga; the Australian media market is very far away, and it was tough for them to find new U.S investors to step in and roll up their sleeves," said one analyst, adding, "The bonds had the feel of being damaged goods."
Salomon Brothers and Toronto Dominion officials declined to comment.
The offering consisted of $150 million in senior secured bonds which will not pay cash interest for four years, as well as warrants to purchase 4.82 percent of the company.

Market sources said the underwriters were only able to place about 30 percent of the offering among high-yield accounts in the U.S. They said the underwriters themselves were forced to purchase some 20 percent of the offering.

The remainder, approximately 40 percent to 50 percent, was purchased by two of the company's equity investors, Lenfest Communications Inc, a U.S. cable company, and Kerry Packer, an Australian media mogul, the sources added.
Lenfest officials did not return calls. Packer could not be reached for comment.
Market sources said the coupon on the bond was 15 percent, which is considered a very attractive yield. But price talk on the issue was originally 15-1/2 percent, they added.

Analysts speculated that despite hefty yield on the bonds, investors were unwilling to purchase the securities for a combination of factors, including poor secondary market performance of the company's prior bond issues.
Standard and Poor's lowered Australis' corporate credit rating to CCC-plus from B-minus earlier this month.

One analyst noted, "There have been a lot of zero-coupon media and telecommunicions deals coming out in the last few months, so many accounts are already loaded up on this type of paper. They're being more selective."
